payload.comment: Preprocessing stage is structurally sound and internally consistent. All split sizes (train 89 996 / val 10 004 / test 7 180) match the official PathMNIST manifest exactly; no subsampling was applied; SHA-256 index hashes, archive MD5, and Zenodo data reference are all present and consistent across the dataset_manifest, split_manifest, and ingestion artefacts. The full 107 180-sample dataset was profiled with zero blank images and zero duplicate train samples. The representation plan (standardize normalization using train-only stats, 4× augmentation via hflip/vflip/brightness) is reasonable for 28×28 H&E patches, and the augmented train size (359 984 = 89 996 × 4) is arithmetically correct. The test-domain shift (CRC-VAL-7K external center) and the resulting class-prevalence skew (adipose ×1.79, debris ×0.41, stroma ×0.56) are thoroughly documented in both the data_profile and the dataset_manifest, with appropriate caveats about small per-class test counts and label ambiguity at patch resolution. No deterministic findings were raised. The sole recurring concern across ingestion and profiling is LLM metadata: llm_model_digest is null and the identifier 'qwen3.8' does not follow standard Qwen naming conventions (e.g. qwen2.5-72b-instruct). This does not affect the correctness of the preprocessing artefacts but limits full reproducibility of any LLM-assisted decisions. Recommend recording the exact model revision/digest before downstream stages that may rely on LLM outputs. The ingestion reviewer's 'revise' action is attributable to this metadata gap rather than to any data-integrity defect; since all deterministic checks pass and the data pipeline is correct, the stage can proceed with the warning noted.
llm_issues: llm_model_digest is null; the exact Qwen model revision used for LLM-assisted decisions cannot be verified or reproduced in downstream stages
llm_model identifier 'qwen3.8' is atypical for the Qwen naming convention; confirm it is the intended tag and not a typo for e.g. qwen2.5 or qwen3-8b

Test split originates from a different clinical center (CRC-VAL-HE-7K); downstream evaluation must report per-class metrics with this domain shift explicitly noted to avoid over-optimistic generalisation claims

Test-set class distribution deviates substantially from train/val (adipose ×1.79, debris ×0.41, stroma ×0.56, smooth muscle ×0.61); small per-class test counts (debris n=339, stroma n=421, smooth muscle n=592) make per-class test metrics statistically noisy—consider confidence intervals or bootstrap in reporting
Brightness augmentation on H&E patches may alter the characteristic hematoxylin/eosin colour balance; verify that the brightness range is constrained to preserve histological colour fidelity

Label ambiguity for 'debris', 'background', 'cancer-associated stroma' vs 'smooth muscle' at 28×28 patch resolution is a known limitation; downstream model selection and reporting should account for this
